thread.title: McDonald's bests Nike, Apple as most visible brand on social media

author: Gina Hall
title: McDonald's bests Nike, Apple as most visible brand on social media
text: – Correspondent, Chicago Business Journal Jan 30, 2018, 11:23am HST McDonald’s reigns as the most visible brand on Twitter and Instagram, beating out the likes of Nike , Coca-Cola , Google and Apple. The Oak Brook, Illinois-based fast food chain’s logo, on average, is featured in almost 890,000 Twitter and Instagram posts per month, according to Statista, an online statistics, market research and business intelligence hub. The researchers associated the popularity of the Golden Arches with the number food-related photos on social-media platforms. “Probably thanks to the 21st century need of taking pictures of our food, McDonald’s (NYSE: MCD) is the surprise winner in this category,” Felix Richter , a Statista data journalist wrote in a blog post accompanying the data. Nike (NYSE: NKE) came in second on the list, as the brand's logo is featured, on average, in 788,490 monthly posts. Adidas's (OTC: ADDDF, ADDYY) logo came in third with 772,520 posts. The study credited the popularity of fitness selfies and athletes’ posts with the prolific number of sportswear impressions. Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO) and Emirates Airline rounded out the Top 5 on the list. “Selfie culture along with the rise of influencers is giving brands a ton of exposure, which, in many cases, they don’t even have to pay for,” Richter noted. Surprisingly, tech brands such as Google (NASDAQ: GOOG), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) ranked well below McDonald’s. Each of the tech brands were featured in less than half a million posts. “One could have thought that all those iPhone mirror selfies would have propelled Apple further up in the ranking,” Richter observed. McDonald’s presence atop the social media sphere is surprising considering its current issues. The classic fast food chain has lost a significant portion of its market share to rival chains in the past few years. The company admitted during its investor conference last year that its restaurants had lost 500 million sales transactions since 2012. But as the social media stats suggest, the company may not be as out of touch with the younger generation as many might expect. McDonald’s has made several recent efforts to appeal to younger consumers concerned with the company’s social responsibility. As part of this shift, the chain plans to recycle packaging at most of its restaurants worldwide by 2025. The company is also putting fresh meat into two of its burgers in an effort to appeal to those who are concerned about the taste and nutritional value of its patties.
